Create the cover illustration for a children's picture book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: In the dewy meadow of the Little Farm, the Cow stands calmly chewing a mouthful of grass while the Rooster, the Cuckoo and the Black Grouse sit in a row along her broad back, each one puffing out his chest and looking very pleased, as if she belonged to him alone. The Cow rolls her eyes up towards them with a patient look. Fresh early-morning light, with the cowshed and the birch wood behind.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Cow: A gentle, sturdy old Norwegian farm cow with a glossy reddish-brown coat, a broad white stripe running all along her back and down her tail, a white belly, white-speckled legs, a pink nose, big, calm brown eyes with long dark eyelashes, and two short, pale, upward-curving horns. A small brass bell hangs on a leather strap around her neck. She chews her cud slowly and never hurries.
- the Rooster: A sleek, swaggering rooster with jet-black plumage that shimmers beetle-green in the sun, a tall, jagged scarlet comb standing straight up, long dangling wattles, small white earlobes, fiery orange eyes, a sharp slate-grey beak, slate-grey legs with long toes, and a fountain of long, curving green-black sickle feathers for a tail. He struts about with his head held high and loves the sound of his own voice.
- the Cuckoo: A slim, sleek cuckoo, smaller than a rooster, with a smooth ash-blue-grey head, back and wings, a white belly finely barred with thin dark stripes, a long, rounded dark-grey tail edged with little white spots, bright yellow rings around his round, sleepy, half-closed eyes, a short, slightly curved dark beak with a yellow base, and small yellow feet. One tuft of feathers always sticks up on the back of his head.
- the Black Grouse: A large, calm black grouse cock, a little bigger than a rooster, with glossy blue-black plumage, a bright-red fleshy arch like an eyebrow above each eye, a white bar across each wing, a fluffy snow-white puff of feathers under his tail, and a lyre-shaped tail whose two outer feathers curl outwards like hooks. He has feathered grey legs, a short black beak and wise, kind dark eyes, and stands tall and dignified like a judge.

Setting:
- the Little Farm: A small farm at the edge of a birch wood: a low grey log cowshed with a grass roof and a wide doorway, a little wooden ladder leading up to a hen hatch in its wall, a big, soft heap of golden straw against its side, a tall, weathered wooden gatepost with a flat top beside the straw, a grey split-rail fence, a dewy green meadow sloping down to white-stemmed birches, and a purple-brown heather moor rising on the hill beyond.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, where farm animals and wild birds can talk. On a small farm at the edge of a birch wood, the rooster, the cuckoo and the black grouse have bought one cow together. The rooster's home is a little hen hatch with a ladder in the cowshed wall, the cuckoo's home is a tall birch tree in the wood, and the black grouse's home is the purple-brown heather moor on the hill above. At night the three birds sleep on the big heap of golden straw beside the cowshed, next to the cow. The birds and the cow are natural animals without clothes.

This story's season, light and colours: Sunrise on an early-summer morning: a blazing saffron-and-gold sky with the sun coming up over the heather moor, long cool-blue shadows, thin silver mist lying in the hollows, and every feather rimmed with golden light. The opening picture is set in soft, warm afternoon light instead.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

illustrations.caption: «Nå er kua mi!» galer Hanen, og Gjøken skvetter opp i halmen.
illustrations.alt: Det er soloppgang. Hanen står på en høy stolpe og galer. Nedenfor skvetter Gjøken opp av halmen, mens Århanen sover videre med hodet under vingen og Kua ligger og tygger.

- the Little Farm: A small farm at the edge of a birch wood: a low grey log cowshed with a grass roof and a wide doorway, a little wooden ladder leading up to a hen hatch in its wall, a big, soft heap of golden straw against its side, a tall, weathered wooden gatepost with a flat top beside the straw, a grey split-rail fence, a dewy green meadow sloping down to white-stemmed birches, and a purple-brown heather moor rising on the hill beyond.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, where farm animals and wild birds can talk. On a small farm at the edge of a birch wood, the rooster, the cuckoo and the black grouse have bought one cow together. The rooster's home is a little hen hatch with a ladder in the cowshed wall, the cuckoo's home is a tall birch tree in the wood, and the black grouse's home is the purple-brown heather moor on the hill above. At night the three birds sleep on the big heap of golden straw beside the cowshed, next to the cow. The birds and the cow are natural animals without clothes.

This story's season, light and colours: Sunrise on an early-summer morning: a blazing saffron-and-gold sky with the sun coming up over the heather moor, long cool-blue shadows, thin silver mist lying in the hollows, and every feather rimmed with golden light. The opening picture is set in soft, warm afternoon light instead.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Gentle and safe for young children: no blood, wounds or gore, and no violence in progress. Show danger with mood, posture and distance, never with injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.
